warnings: Texas experienced a significant measles outbreak beginning in early 2025, particularly in West Texas; case counts may be large and rapidly evolving — prioritize most recent official updates.
Texas DSHS may publish situation reports or health alerts specific to this outbreak; these are highest-priority sources.
CDC 'Measles Cases and Outbreaks' page is updated frequently during active outbreaks and should be checked for the most current cumulative totals.
County-level data may be suppressed or aggregated by DSHS for privacy when case counts are small (<5); note suppression in records.
Multiple local health departments (Dallas, Harris, Tarrant, El Paso, Bexar counties) may publish independent updates — reconcile with state totals.
Unvaccinated population clusters (e.g., religious or philosophical exemption communities) are epidemiologically significant context for Texas outbreaks.
Importation status (international vs. domestic) should be captured if reported, as it affects outbreak classification.

Time window (2025-01-01 to 2025-04-30) spans an active outbreak period; expect frequent updates and version changes in official reports — timestamp each source retrieval.
MMWR reports may cover multi-state outbreaks; filter carefully for Texas-specific data and avoid attributing multi-state totals to Texas alone.
